Q 48:25 · Vol. 4, pp. 342–344

Verse 25

The verse as the commentary quotes it
They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the sacrificial animals were prevented from reaching their place of sacrifice. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you might trample them and thus there would befall you from them dishonor without knowledge - that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been apart, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment (25)
هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ وَالْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفاً أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ وَنِساءٌ مُؤْمِناتٌ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ فَتُصِيبَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ مَعَرَّةٌ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً (25)
Vol. 4, p. 342
. It was read: wa-l-hadya and wa-l-hadyi, with the ya' lightened and doubled; it is what is sent as an offering to the Ka'ba: in the accusative, joined to the accusative pronoun in 'barred you,' i.e., they barred you and barred the sacrificial animals; and in the genitive, joined to 'al-Masjid al-Haram,' meaning: and they barred you from slaughtering the offering 'a-'kufan that it reach its place,' i.e., held back from being sacrificed; and in the nominative, meaning: and the offering was barred. And its 'mahill' is: its place in which its slaughter is lawful, i.e., obligatory. This is evidence for Abu Hanifa that the place for the offering of one who is prevented from the pilgrimage is the Sanctuary.
وقرئ: والهدى، والهدى: بتخفيف الياء وتشديدها، وهو ما يهدى إلى الكعبة: بالنصب عطفا على الضمير المنصوب في صدّوكم. أى: صدّوكم وصدّوا الهدى وبالجر عطفا على المسجد الحرام. بمعنى: وصدّوكم عن نحر الهدى مَعْكُوفاً أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ محبوسا عن أن يباع، وبالرفع على: وصدّ الهدى. ومحله: مكانه الذي يحل فيه نحره، أى يجب. وهذا دليل لأبى حنيفة على أن المحصر محل هديه الحرم.
Question
If you say: how did the Messenger of God ﷺ and those with him leave ihram when their offerings were slaughtered only at al-Hudaybiya?
فإن قلت: فكيف حل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه وإنما نحر هديهم بالحديبية؟
Answer
I say: part of al-Hudaybiya is of the Sanctuary. It is also related that the tents of the Messenger of God ﷺ were in the non-sacred area and his place of prayer in the Sanctuary.
قلت: بعض الحديبية من الحرم «1» . وروى أن مضارب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت في الحل، ومصلاه في الحرم «2» .
Question
If you say: then he did slaughter in the Sanctuary, so why was it said 'prevented from reaching its place'?
فإن قلت: فإذن قد نحر في الحرم، فلم قيل: مَعْكُوفاً أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ؟
Answer
I say: what is meant is the customary place, which is Mina. 'Whom you did not know' is an attribute of both the men and the women. And 'that you might trample them' is an inclusive substitution from them or from the pronoun
قلت: المراد المحل المعهود وهو منى لَمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ صفة الرجال والنساء جميعا. وأَنْ تَطَؤُهُمْ بدل اشتمال منهم أو من الضمير
Vol. 4, p. 343
in 'you knew them.' And 'al-ma'arra' is on the pattern maf'ala, from 'arrahu meaning 'arahu, when something he dislikes and which is hard on him befalls him. And 'without knowledge' is connected to 'that you might trample them,' meaning: that you trample them not knowing them. Trampling and treading are an expression for striking down and destroying. He said: 'You trampled us with a trampling in anger, like the trampling of a hobbled camel on young, green hurum.' And the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'The last trampling that God trampled was at Wajj.' The meaning: that there were in Mecca some Muslims mixed with the polytheists, not distinguished from them nor with known locations, so it was said: had it not been for the dislike that you destroy believing people among the polytheists while you do not know them, and that harm and hardship would then befall you through their destruction, He would not have withheld your hands from them. The answer to 'lawla' is omitted because the speech indicates it. It is also possible that 'if they had been apart' is like a repetition of 'if not for believing men,' because they return to one meaning, with 'We would have punished' being the answer.
المنصوب في تعلموهم. والمعرة: مفعلة، من عره بمعنى عراه إذا دهاه «1» ما يكره ويشق عليه. وبِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ متعلق بأن تطؤهم، يعنى: أن تطئوهم غير عالمين بهم. والوطء والدوس: عبارة عن الإيقاع والإبادة. قال: ووطئتنا وطأ على حنق … وطأ المقيّد نابت الهرم «2» وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وأن آخر وطأة وطئها الله بوج» «3» والمعنى: أنه كان بمكة قوم من المسلمين مختلطون بالمشركين غير متميزين منهم ولا معروفى الأماكن فقيل: ولولا كراهة أن تهلكوا ناسا مؤمنين بين ظهراني المشركين وأنتم غير عارفين بهم، فتصيبكم بإهلاكهم مكروه ومشقة: لما كف أيديكم عنهم، وحذف جواب «لولا» لدلالة الكلام عليه «4» . ويجوز أن يكون لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا كالتكرير للولا رجال مؤمنون، لمرجعهما إلى معنى واحد، ويكون لَعَذَّبْنَا هو الجواب.
Question
If you say: what dishonor would befall them if they killed them without knowing?
فإن قلت: أى معرة تصيبهم إذا قتلوهم وهم لا يعلمون.
Answer
I say: the blood-money and expiation would become due for them, and the polytheists' evil talk that they did to the people of their own religion the like of what they did to us without distinction, and the sin if some negligence occurred from them.
قلت: يصيبهم وجوب الدية والكفارة، وسوء قالة المشركين أنهم فعلوا بأهل دينهم مثل ما فعلوا بنا من غير تمييز، والمأثم إذا جرى منهم بعض التقصير.
Question
If you say: His words 'that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills' are a reason for what?
فإن قلت: قوله تعالى لِيُدْخِلَ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ تعليل لماذا؟
Answer
I say: for what the verse indicates and was brought for:
قلت: لما دلت عليه الآية وسيقت له:
Vol. 4, p. 344
of the withholding of hands from the people of Mecca and the prevention of killing them, to protect those of the believers among them, as if He said: the withholding and prevention of punishment was so that God might admit into His mercy, i.e., into His granting of success toward increase of good and obedience, their believers; or that there might enter into Islam those of their polytheists who desired it. 'If they had been apart': if they had separated and some had been distinguished from others, from zalahu yazilu. It was read: law tazayalu.
من كف الأيدى عن أهل مكة، والمنع من قتلهم، صونا لمن بين أظهرهم من المؤمنين، كأنه قال: كان الكف ومنع التعذيب ليدخل الله في رحمته، أى: في توفيقه لزيادة الخير والطاعة مؤمنيهم. أو ليدخل في الإسلام من رغب فيه من مشركيهم لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لو تفرقوا وتميز بعضهم من بعض: من زاله يزيله. وقرئ: لو تزايلوا.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 342
1. (1) . Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ went out intending 'umra, and the disbelievers of Quraysh stood between him and the House, so he slaughtered his offering and shaved his head at al-Hudaybiya.' And in it, from the narration of al-Miswar and Marwan: 'that he ﷺ said to his Companions: Rise, slaughter, then shave.' Al-Bukhari said: and al-Hudaybiya is outside the Sanctuary. [.....]
2. . Ahmad related it from the narration of al-Miswar and Marwan, in the course of the long hadith, saying: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray in the Sanctuary while his tent was pitched in the non-sacred area.'
1. (1) . أخرجه البخاري من حديث ابن عمر قال: «خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم معتمرا فحال كفار قريش بينه وبين البيت، فنحر هديه وحلق رأسه بالحديبية» وفيه من رواية المسور ومروان «أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه: قوموا فانحروا ثم احلقوا» قال البخاري: والحديبية خارج الحرم. [.....]
2. . أخرجه أحمد من رواية المسور ومروان. في أثناء الحديث الطويل. قال «وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلى في الحرم. وهو مضطرب في الحل»
Vol. 4, p. 343
1. (1) . His words 'meaning 'arahu when something befalls him': the wording of al-Sihah verbatim: 'he 'urru his people,' i.e., brings upon them something unpleasant with which he smears them. And al-ma'arra is sin. (Editor)
2. . 'And you trampled us with a trampling in anger ... like the trampling of a hobbled one on young hurum, and you left us as meat on a butcher's board, if you were sparing of meat ...' By al-Harith ibn Wa'la al-Dhuhli. 'Al-wat'' is placing the foot upon something forcefully, and it is a metonymy for destruction. 'Al-hanaq' (like sabab) is rancor and rage. 'Al-hurum' (with sukun) is a kind of salty plant that camels graze, and a camel that grazes it is called harim. He says: you came to us exalted over us by your strength and the severity of your onslaught, like the trampling of a hobbled camel on growing hurum, i.e., newly grown; it is also related 'dry hurum,' and he destroys it by his size and strength despite the moisture of that plant and its weakness, or despite its dryness, so that it crumbles. He made him hobbled so that his blow would be strong, since he lifts both legs together and strikes with them when leaping; or he made him hobbled because the humbled one, when he gains power, does not pardon. 'Al-wadm' is the butcher's table on which meat is cut. 'Law' is conditional, whose answer is indicated by his words 'you left us,' i.e.: supposing you had spared a remnant here, you left us like this meat prepared for eating. In the use of 'law' is an indication that he spared none of them.
3. . It was given earlier at the end of Bara'a (al-Tawba).
4. . Mahmud said: 'It is possible that the answer of lawla is omitted ... etc.' Ahmad said: They return here to one meaning even though 'lawla' indicates the prevention of one thing because of the existence of another, and 'law' indicates the prevention of one thing because of the prevention of another, and between these two there is an apparent contradiction, because 'lawla' here entered upon an existent, and 'law' entered upon 'if they had been apart,' which returns to the non-existence of their existence, and the prevention of non-existence is existence; so they come to one thing from this angle. My grandfather ؒ used to favor this second aspect and called it 'tatriya' (refreshing), and it occurs most when speech is long and its beginning is far off and it is necessary to return the end to the beginning, so at times it is refreshed with its wording and at times with another wording conveying the same sense. Its like has been mentioned before. And God knows best. He is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . قوله «بمعنى عراه إذا دهاه» عبارة الصحاح بلفظها: هو يعر قومه: أى يدخل عليهم مكروها يلطخهم به. والمعرة: الإثم. (ع)
2. . ووطئتنا وطأ على حنق
…. وطأ المقيد نابت الهرم وتركتنا لحما على وضم
…. لو كنت تستبقى من اللحم للحرث بن وعلة الذهلي. والوطء: وضع القدم فوق الشيء بشدة. وهو كناية عن الإهلال. والحنق- كسبب، الحقد والغيظ. والهرم- بالسكون-: ضرب من الحمض ترعاه الإبل، وبعير هارم: يرعى الهرم. يقول: أتيتنا مرتفعا علينا بقوتك وشدة بطشك كوطء الجمل المقيد للهرم النابت: أى الحديث النبات. ويروى: يابس الهرم فيهلكه لعظمه وقوته، مع رطوبة ذلك النبات وضعفه، أو مع يبسه فيتفتت، فجعله مقيدا لتكون بطشته قوية، حيث يرفع رجليه معا ويضربها عند الوثوب. أو جعله مقيدا، لأن الذليل إذا قدر لا يعفو. والوضم: خوان الجزار الذي يقطع عليه اللحم. و «لو» شرطية، جوابها دل عليه قوله «تركتنا» أى: على فرض أنك تركت هنا بقية تركتنا كهذا اللحم الذي يهيأ للأكل. وفي التعبير بلو: دلالة على أنه لم يستبق منهم.
3. . تقدم في آخر براءة.
4. . قال محمود: «يجوز أن يكون جواب لولا محذوفا
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وإنما كان مرجعهما هاهنا واحدا وإن كانت لولا تدل على امتناع لوجود، و «لو» تدل على امتناع لامتناع، وبين هذين تناف ظاهر، لأن لولا هاهنا دخلت على وجود، ولو دخلت على قوله تزيلوا وهو راجع إلى عدم وجودهم وامتناع عدم الوجود وجود، فآلا إلى أمر واحد من هذا الوجه. وكان جدي رحمه الله يختار هذا الوجه الثاني ويسميه تطرية، وأكثر ما تكون إذا تطاول الكلام وبعد عهد أوله واحتيج إلى رد الآخر على الأول، فمرة يطرى بلفظه، ومرة بلفظ آخر يؤدى مؤداه. وقد تقدمت لها أمثال، والله أعلم. وهو الموفق.
Vol. 4, p. 344
1. (1) . Al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Dala'il from the narration of 'Urwa in the story of al-Hudaybiya. And in it: 'then Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn 'Amr ... etc.' at length. And the story is in the Sahih from the narration of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib and from the narration of Marwan and al-Miswar. And in al-Nasa'i abbreviated from the narration of Thabit al-Yamani from 'Abd God ibn Mughaffal.
1. (1) . أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل من رواية عروة في قصة الحديبية. وفيه ثم بعثت قريش سهيل بن عمرو الخ مطولا. والقصة في الصحيح من رواية البراء بن عازب ومن رواية مروان والمسور. وفي النسائي مختصرة من رواية ثابت اليماني عن عبد الله بن مغفل.

Q 48:26 · Vol. 4, pp. 344–345

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
When those who disbelieved set in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And God is ever, of all things, Knowing (26)
إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى وَكانُوا أَحَقَّ بِها وَأَهْلَها وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً (26)
Vol. 4, p. 344
. 'When': what precedes it may operate on it, i.e., 'We would have punished them' or 'they barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram' at that time; and it may be accusative by an implied 'remember.' What is meant by the zealotry of those who disbelieved and the tranquility of the believers (zealotry being pride and tranquility being dignity) is what is related: that when the Messenger of God ﷺ alighted at al-Hudaybiya, Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn 'Amr al-Qurashi, Huwaytib ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza and Mikraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Akhyaf to propose to the Prophet ﷺ that he return that same year, on condition that Quraysh would vacate Mecca for him the following year for three days. He did that, and they wrote a document between them. He ﷺ said to 'Ali ؓ: Write: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Suhayl and his companions said: We do not know this; write rather: In Your name, O God. Then he said: Write: 'This is what the Messenger of God ﷺ has made peace upon with the people of Mecca.' They said: If we knew you were the Messenger of God we would not have barred you from the House nor fought you; write rather: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd God has made peace upon with the people of Mecca. He ﷺ said: Write what they want, for I bear witness that I am the Messenger of God and I am Muhammad ibn 'Abd God. The Muslims were about to refuse this and recoil from it, so God sent down tranquility upon His Messenger and they became dignified and forbearing. 'The word of righteousness' is 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and 'Muhammad is the Messenger of God': God chose it for His Prophet and for those with him, the people of goodness and its deserving ones, and those who are more worthy of guidance than others. It is also said: it is the word of testimony. From al-Hasan ؓ: the word of righteousness is fulfillment of the covenant. The meaning of its annexation to righteousness is that it is the cause and foundation of righteousness. It is also said: the word of the people of righteousness. And in the codex of al-Harith ibn Suwayd, companion of 'Abd God: wa-kanu ahlaha wa-ahaqqa biha; he is the one who buried his codex in the days of al-Hajjaj.
إِذْ يجوز أن يعمل فيه ما قبله. أى: لعذبناهم أو صدوهم عن المسجد الحرام في ذلك الوقت، وأن ينتصب بإضمار اذكر. والمراد بحمية الذين كفروا وسكينة المؤمنين- والحمية الأنفة والسكينة الوقار- ما روى أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزل بالحديبية بعثت قريش سهيل بن عمرو القرشي وحويطب بن عبد العزى ومكرز بن حفص بن الأخيف، على أن يعرضوا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يرجع من عامه ذلك على أن تخلى له قريش مكة من العام القابل ثلاثة أيام، ففعل ذلك، «1» وكتبوا بينهم كتابا، فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام لعلى رضى الله عنه: اكتب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، فقال سهيل وأصحابه: ما نعرف هذا، ولكن اكتب: باسمك اللهم، ثم قال: اكتب «هذا ما صالح عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل مكة» فقالوا: لو كنا نعلم أنك رسول الله ما صددناك عن البيت ولا قاتلناك، ولكن اكتب: هذا ما صالح عليه محمد بن عبد الله أهل مكة، فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام: اكتب ما يريدون، فأنا أشهد أنى رسول الله وأنا محمد بن عبد الله، فهمّ المسلمون أن يأبوا ذلك ويشمئزوا منه، فأنزل الله على رسوله السكينة فتوقروا وحلموا. وكَلِمَةَ التَّقْوى بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ومحمد رسول الله: قد اختارها الله لنبيه وللذين معه أهل الخير ومستحقيه ومن هم أولى بالهداية من غيرهم. وقيل: هي كلمة الشهادة. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: كلمة التقوى هي الوفاء بالعهد. ومعنى إضافتها إلى التقوى: أنها سبب التقوى وأساسها. وقيل: كلمة أهل التقوى. وفي مصحف الحرث بن سويد صاحب عبد الله: وكانوا أهلها وأحق بها، وهو الذي دفن مصحفه أيام الحجاج.
Vol. 4, p. 345
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 344

And the story is in the Sahih from the narration of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib and from the narration of Marwan and al-Miswar. And in al-Nasa'i abbreviated from the narration of Thabit al-Yamani from 'Abd God ibn Mughaffal.

1. (1) . I did not find it explained in this form. Al-Tabari related, from the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on His words 'Certainly has God shown the truth of His Messenger's vision ... (the verse)': the Prophet ﷺ said to them: 'I have seen that you will enter al-Masjid al-Haram with your heads shaved and hair shortened.' When he left al-Hudaybiya and did not enter that year, the hypocrites criticized this. They said: Where is his vision? So God said 'Certainly has God shown the truth of His Messenger's vision ... (the verse).' And al-Tabari related, by the route of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, who said: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ was shown, while at al-Hudaybiya, that he and his Companions would enter among the people of Mecca with heads shaved. When he slaughtered the offering at al-Hudaybiya, his Companions said: Where is your vision, O Messenger of God? So it was revealed.' And by it he said, and His words 'and has placed before that a near victory' he said: the slaughter at al-Hudaybiya; so they returned and conquered Khaybar. He said: then he performed 'umra after that, so the fulfillment of his vision was in the following year.
2. . His words 'i.e., He was truthful to him in the vision, joined (multabisan)' probably should read 'multabisatan' (feminine). (Editor)
1. (1) . لم أجده هكذا مفسرا وروى الطبري من روآية عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في قوله لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ- الآية فقال لهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «إنى قد رأيت أنكم ستدخلون المسجد الحرام محلقين رؤسكم ومقصرين. فلما ترك الحديبية ولم يدخل ذلك العام طعن المنافقون في ذلك. فقالوا: أين رؤياه، فقال الله لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا- الآية وروى الطبري من طريق ابن أبى نجيح عن مجاهد قال «أرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بالحديبية أنه يدخل في أهل مكة هو وأصحابه محلقين فلما نحر الهدى وهو بالحديبية قال أصحابه: أين رؤياك يا رسول الله؟ فنزلت» وبه قال وقوله فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً قال: النحر بالحديبية، فرجعوا ففتحوا خيبرا. وقال: ثم اعتمر بعد ذلك فكان تصديق رؤياه في السنة المقبلة» .
2. . قوله «أى صدقه الرؤيا ملتبسا» لعله: ملتبسة. (ع)

Q 48:27 · Vol. 4, pp. 345–346

Verse 27

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Certainly has God shown the truth of His Messenger's vision: 'You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing.' He knew what you did not know and has placed before that a near victory (27)
لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُؤُسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لا تَخافُونَ فَعَلِمَ ما لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً (27)
Vol. 4, p. 345
. The Messenger of God ﷺ saw before his departure to al-Hudaybiya as if he and his Companions had entered Mecca in security, having shaved and shortened. He related the vision to his Companions, and they rejoiced and were glad, thinking that they would enter it in that year, and said: The Messenger of God's vision is true. When that was delayed, 'Abd God ibn Ubayy, 'Abd God ibn Nufayl and Rifa'a ibn al-Harith said: By God, we have not shaved nor shortened nor seen al-Masjid al-Haram; so it was revealed. The meaning of 'God has shown the truth of His Messenger's vision' is that He was truthful to him in his vision and did not belie him (exalted is God above lying and above everything ugly, greatly exalted), so the preposition was dropped and the verb made to reach its object directly, like the words of the Exalted 'who were true to what they promised God' (al-Ahzab 33:23).
رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل خروجه إلى الحديبية كأنه وأصحابه قد دخلوا مكة آمنين وقد حلقوا وقصروا، فقصّ الرؤيا على أصحابه، ففرحوا واستبشروا وحسبوا أنهم داخلوها في عامهم، وقالوا: إن رؤيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حق، فلما تأخر ذلك قال عبد الله بن أبىّ وعبد الله بن نفيل ورفاعة بن الحرث: والله ما حلقنا ولا قصرنا ولا رأينا المسجد الحرام «1» فنزلت. ومعنى صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا صدقه في رؤياه ولم يكذبه- تعالى الله عن الكذب وعن كل قبيح علوا كبيرا- فحذف الجارّ وأوصل الفعل، كقوله تعالى: صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه.
Question
If you say: to what is 'in truth' connected?
فإن قلت: بم تعلق بِالْحَقِّ؟
Answer
I say: either to 'sadaqa,' i.e., He was truthful to him in what he saw, and in its coming to pass truthfully, joined with the truth, i.e., with a sound purpose and consummate wisdom, namely the testing in it and the distinction between the sincere believer and one in whose heart is sickness. It is also possible that it connects to the vision as a circumstantial clause from it, i.e., He was truthful to him in the vision, joined with truth, meaning that it was not among jumbled dreams. It is also possible that 'bi-l-haqq' is an oath: either by the truth that is the opposite of falsehood, or by the Truth which is among His names, and 'you will surely enter' is its answer. On the first it is the answer of an omitted oath.
قلت: إمّا بصدق، أى: صدقه فيما رأى، وفي كونه وحصوله صدقا ملتبسا بالحق: أى بالغرض الصحيح والحكمة البالغة، وذلك ما فيه من الابتلاء والتمييز بين المؤمن المخلص، وبين من في قلبه مرض. ويجوز أن يتعلق بالرؤيا حالا منها أى: صدقه الرؤيا ملتبسا «2» بالحق، على معنى أنها لم تكن من أضغاث الأحلام. ويجوز أن يكون بِالْحَقِّ قسما: إمّا بالحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل. أو بالحق الذي هو من أسمائه. ولَتَدْخُلُنَّ جوابه. وعلى الأوّل هو جواب قسم محذوف.
Question
If you say: what is the reason for the entry of 'if God wills' into the reports of God, Mighty and Majestic?
فإن قلت: ما وجه دخول إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ في أخبار الله عز وجل؟
Answer
I say: there are several aspects: that He makes His promise conditional on the will, teaching His servants to say likewise in their promises, observing God's courtesy and following His practice; and that He means: you will surely all enter, if God wills and none of you has died; or that it was upon the tongue of an angel, so the angel inserted 'if God wills'; or it is a relating of what the Messenger of God ﷺ said to his Companions and related to them. It is also said: it is connected to 'secure.' 'He knew what you did not know' of the wisdom and correctness in delaying the conquest of Mecca to the following year
قلت: فيه وجوه: أن يعلق عدته بالمشيئة تعليما لعباده أن يقولوا في عداتهم مثل ذلك، متأدّبين بأدب الله، ومقتدين بسنته، وأن يريد: لتدخلنّ جميعا إن شاء الله ولم يمت منكم أحدا، أو كان ذلك على لسان ملك، فأدخل الملك إن شاء الله. أو هي حكاية ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحابه وقصّ عليهم. وقيل: هو متعلق بآمنين فَعَلِمَ ما لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا من الحكمة والصواب في تأخير فتح مكة إلى العام القابل
Vol. 4, p. 346
'He placed before that' i.e., short of the conquest of Mecca, 'a near victory,' which is the conquest of Khaybar, so that the hearts of the believers might find relief in it until the promised conquest was made easy.
فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ أى من دون فتح مكة فَتْحاً قَرِيباً وهو فتح خيبر، لتستروح إليه قلوب المؤمنين إلى أن يتيسر الفتح الموعود.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 345
1. (1) . I did not find it explained in this form. Al-Tabari related, from the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on His words 'Certainly has God shown the truth of His Messenger's vision ... (the verse)': the Prophet ﷺ said to them: 'I have seen that you will enter al-Masjid al-Haram with your heads shaved and hair shortened.' When he left al-Hudaybiya and did not enter that year, the hypocrites criticized this. They said: Where is his vision? So God said 'Certainly has God shown the truth of His Messenger's vision ... (the verse).' And al-Tabari related, by the route of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, who said: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ was shown, while at al-Hudaybiya, that he and his Companions would enter among the people of Mecca with heads shaved. When he slaughtered the offering at al-Hudaybiya, his Companions said: Where is your vision, O Messenger of God? So it was revealed.' And by it he said, and His words 'and has placed before that a near victory' he said: the slaughter at al-Hudaybiya; so they returned and conquered Khaybar. He said: then he performed 'umra after that, so the fulfillment of his vision was in the following year.
2. . His words 'i.e., He was truthful to him in the vision, joined (multabisan)' probably should read 'multabisatan' (feminine). (Editor)
1. (1) . لم أجده هكذا مفسرا وروى الطبري من روآية عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في قوله لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا بِالْحَقِّ- الآية فقال لهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «إنى قد رأيت أنكم ستدخلون المسجد الحرام محلقين رؤسكم ومقصرين. فلما ترك الحديبية ولم يدخل ذلك العام طعن المنافقون في ذلك. فقالوا: أين رؤياه، فقال الله لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيا- الآية وروى الطبري من طريق ابن أبى نجيح عن مجاهد قال «أرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بالحديبية أنه يدخل في أهل مكة هو وأصحابه محلقين فلما نحر الهدى وهو بالحديبية قال أصحابه: أين رؤياك يا رسول الله؟ فنزلت» وبه قال وقوله فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ فَتْحاً قَرِيباً قال: النحر بالحديبية، فرجعوا ففتحوا خيبرا. وقال: ثم اعتمر بعد ذلك فكان تصديق رؤياه في السنة المقبلة» .
2. . قوله «أى صدقه الرؤيا ملتبسا» لعله: ملتبسة. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 346
1. (1) . His words 'that He will make your religion prevail (dinak)' probably should read 'his religion (dinahu),' as al-Nasafi's wording. (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «إنه سيظهر دينك» لعله: دينه، كعبارة النسفي. (ع)
21
Q 48:28 · Vol. 4, p. 346

Verse 28

The verse as the commentary quotes it
It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion. And sufficient is God as Witness (28)
هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً (28)
Vol. 4, p. 346
. 'With guidance and the religion of truth': with the religion of Islam. 'To manifest it': to raise it 'over all religion,' over the genus of all religion, meaning the various religions of the polytheists and the deniers among the People of the Book. He, glory be to Him, has made that true, for you will never see a religion except that Islam has above it might and dominance. It is also said: that is at the descent of Jesus, when no disbeliever remains on the face of the earth. It is also said: it is its manifestation by proofs and signs. And in this verse is a reinforcement of what He promised of the conquest and a settling of the souls of the believers that God the Exalted will open for them lands and will provide for them such dominance over regions that the conquest of Mecca will seem slight to them. 'And sufficient is God as Witness' that what He promised will come to pass. From al-Hasan ؓ: He bore witness against Himself that He would make your religion prevail.
بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ بدين الإسلام لِيُظْهِرَهُ ليعليه عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ على جنس الدين كله، يريد: الأديان المختلفة من أديان المشركين والجاحدين من أهل الكتاب: ولقد حقق ذلك سبحانه، فإنك لا ترى دينا قط إلا وللإسلام دونه العز والغلبة. وقيل: هو عند نزول عيسى حين لا يبقى على وجه الأرض كافر. وقيل: هو إظهاره بالحجج والآيات. وفي هذه الآية تأكيد لما وعد من الفتح وتوطين لنفوس المؤمنين على أنّ الله تعالى سيفتح لهم من البلاد ويقيض لهم من الغلبة على الأقاليم ما يستقلون إليه فتح مكة وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً على أنّ ما وعده كائن. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: شهد على نفسه أنه سيظهر دينك «1»
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 346
1. (1) . His words 'that He will make your religion prevail (dinak)' probably should read 'his religion (dinahu),' as al-Nasafi's wording. (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «إنه سيظهر دينك» لعله: دينه، كعبارة النسفي. (ع)
22
Q 48:29 · Vol. 4, pp. 346–348

Verse 29

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Muhammad is the Messenger of God; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers - so that He may enrage the disbelievers through them. God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward (29)
مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَراهُمْ رُكَّعاً سُجَّداً يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْواناً سِيماهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ ذلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ فَآزَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنْهُمْ مَغْفِرَةً وَأَجْراً عَظِيماً (29)
Vol. 4, p. 346
. 'Muhammad' is either the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., 'He is Muhammad,' because of the preceding 'It is He who sent His Messenger,' or a subject, with 'the Messenger of God' as an explanatory apposition. From Ibn 'Amir that he read 'rasula God' in the accusative, in praise. 'And those with him' are his Companions; 'forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves' are plurals of shadid and rahim. Like it are 'humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers' (al-Ma'ida 5:54), 'and be harsh upon them' (al-Tawba 9:73), and 'to the believers kind and merciful' (al-Tawba 9:128). From al-Hasan ؓ: their severity against the disbelievers reached the point that they guarded their garments from touching the disbelievers' garments and their bodies from touching their bodies, and their mercy toward one another reached the point that no believer saw another believer without shaking his hand and embracing him. As for shaking hands, the jurists did not differ about it; as for embracing, Abu Hanifa ؒ disliked it, and likewise
مُحَمَّدٌ إما خبر مبتدإ، أى: هو محمد لتقدّم قوله تعالى هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ وإما مبتدأ، ورسول الله: عطف بيان. وعن ابن عامر أنه قرأ: رسول الله، بالنصب على المدح وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أصحابه أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ جمع شديد ورحيم. ونحوه أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ، وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ. بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: بلغ من تشدّدهم على الكفار: أنهم كانوا يتحرّزون من ثيابهم أن تلزق بثيابهم، ومن أبدانهم أن تمس أبدانهم، وبلغ من ترحمهم فيما بينهم أنه كان لا يرى مؤمن مؤمنا إلا صافحه وعانقه، والمصافحة لم تختلف فيها الفقهاء. وأما المعانقة فقد كرهها أبو حنيفة رحمه الله، وكذلك
Vol. 4, p. 347
kissing. He said: I do not like that a man kiss another man's face, hand or anything of his body. Abu Yusuf permitted embracing. It is the right of Muslims in every age to observe this severity and this tenderness: to be severe with those not of their community and religion and to avoid them, and to live with their brothers in Islam with tenderness, through kindness, connection, restraint from harm, help, forbearance and easygoing character. The aspect of one who read ashidda'a and ruhama'a in the accusative: that he makes them accusative as praise, or as a circumstantial clause from the implied word in 'ma'ahu,' and makes 'you see them' the predicate. 'Their mark (sima)' is their sign. It was read simau'hum, and it has three dialects: these two, and simiya'. What is meant by it is the mark that appears on the forehead of the much-prostrating person from frequent prostration, and the words of the Exalted 'from the trace of prostration' explain it, i.e., from the effect that prostration produces. Each of the two 'Alis, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin and 'Ali ibn 'Abd God ibn 'Abbas, father of kings, was called 'the one of the calluses,' because their much prostration produced in its places on them things like the calluses of a camel. It was read: min athar al-sujud and min athar al-sujud (plural); and likewise from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it is the mark in the face.
التقبيل. قال لا أحب أن يقبل الرجل من الرجل وجهه ولا يده ولا شيئا من جسده. وقد رخص أبو يوسف في المعانقة. ومن حق المسلمين في كل زمان أن يراعوا هذا التشدّد وهذا التعطف: فيتشدّدوا على من ليس على ملتهم ودينهم ويتحاموه، ويعاشروا إخوتهم في الإسلام متعطفين بالبر والصلة. وكف الأذى، والمعونة، والاحتمال، والأخلاق السجيحة «1» . ووجه من قرأ: أشداء، ورحماء- بالنصب-: أن ينصبهما على المدح، أو على الحال بالمقدّر في مَعَهُ، ويجعل تَراهُمْ الخبر سِيماهُمْ علامتهم. وقرئ سيماؤهم، وفيها ثلاث لغات: هاتان. والسيمياء، والمراد بها السمة التي تحدث في جبهة السجاد من كثرة السجود، وقوله تعالى مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ يفسرها، أى: من التأثير الذي يؤثره السجود، وكان كل من العليين: علىّ بن الحسين زين العابدين، وعلىّ بن عبد الله بن عباس أبى الأملاك، يقال له: ذو الثفنات، لأنّ كثرة سجودهما أحدثت في مواقعه منهما أشباه ثفنات «2» البعير. وقرئ: من أثر السجود، ومن آثار السجود، وكذا عن سعيد ابن جبير: هي السمة في الوجه.
Question
If you say: it came from the Prophet ﷺ: 'Do not mark (la ta'lubu) your faces,' and from Ibn 'Umar ؓ that he saw a man on whose face prostration had left a mark and said: The form of your face is your nose; so do not mark your face nor disfigure your form.
فإن قلت: فقد جاء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «لا تعلبوا «3» صوركم «4» » وعن ابن عمر رضى الله عنه أنه رأى رجلا قد أثر في وجهه السجود فقال: إن صورة وجهك أنفك، فلا تعلب وجهك، ولا تشن صورتك «5» .
Answer
I say: that is when he leans on the ground with his forehead so that this mark is produced on it. That is ostentation and hypocrisy, from which we seek refuge with God; we speak only of what appears on the forehead of the prostrator who prostrates only sincerely for the sake of God the Exalted. From one of the early ones: We used to pray and nothing was seen between our eyes, and now we see one of us pray and there is seen between his eyes the knee of a camel; we do not know whether the heads have grown heavier or the ground rougher. He only meant by that the one who does it deliberately for hypocrisy. It is also said: it is the yellowness of the face from fear of God. From al-Dahhak: it is not the scar on the faces but yellowness. From Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: the dew of ablution and the dust of the ground. From 'Ata' ؒ: their faces were illuminated by the length of
قلت: ذلك إذا اعتمد بجبهته على الأرض لتحدث فيه تلك السمة. وذلك رياء ونفاق يستعاذ بالله منه، ونحن فيما حدث في جبهة السجاد الذي لا يسجد إلا خالصا لوجه الله تعالى. وعن بعض المتقدّمين: كنا نصلى فلا يرى بين أعيننا شيء، ونرى أحدنا الآن يصلى فيرى بين عينيه ركبة البعير، فما ندرى أثقلت الأرؤس أم خشنت الأرض وإنما أراد بذلك من تعمد ذلك للنفاق. وقيل: هو صفرة الوجه من خشية الله. وعن الضحاك: ليس بالندب «6» في الوجوه، ولكنه صفرة. وعن سعيد بن المسيب: ندى الطهور وتراب الأرض. وعن عطاء رحمه الله: استنارت وجوههم من طول
Vol. 4, p. 348
their night prayer, as in the saying: 'Whoever prays much at night, his face is beautiful by day.' 'That' description 'is their description,' i.e., their wondrous description in both Books together; then He began anew, saying 'like a plant,' meaning: they are like a plant. It is also said: the speech was completed at His words 'That is their description in the Torah'; then He began 'And their description in the Gospel is like a plant.' It is also possible that 'that' is a vague pointer clarified by His words 'like a plant which produces its offshoots,' like the words of the Exalted 'And We decreed to him that matter: that the last remnant of these would be cut off by morning' (al-Hijr 15:66). It was read: al-Anjil, with fatha on the hamza. 'Shat'ahu' means its young shoots. One says ash-ta'a al-zar' when it sends out shoots. It was read: shat'ahu, with fatha on the ta'; shat'ahu with the hamza lightened; shata'ahu with madd; shatahu with the hamza dropped and its vowel moved to what precedes; and shatwahu with it turned into waw. 'Fa-azarahu' is from mu'azara, which is assistance. From al-Akhfash: it is af'ala. It was read: fa-azarahu, lightened and doubled, i.e., strengthened its support and fortified it. Whoever takes 'azara' as af'ala, it has the sense of the two readings. 'Fa-staghlaza': it passed from thinness to thickness. 'Fa-stawa 'ala suqihi': it stood straight on its stalk (suq, plural of saq). It is also said: it is written in the Gospel: There will come forth a people who grow as the plant grows, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. From 'Ikrima: it put forth its shoots with Abu Bakr, fortified it with 'Umar, grew thick with 'Uthman, and stood upon its stalk with 'Ali. This is a parable God struck for the beginning of the matter of Islam and its progress in growth until it became strong and firm, because the Prophet ﷺ stood alone; then God strengthened him with those who believed with him, as the first stalk of the plant is strengthened by what surrounds it of what is generated from it, until it delights the sowers.
ما صلوا بالليل، كقوله «من كثرت صلاته بالليل حسن وجهه بالنهار» «1» ذلِكَ الوصف مَثَلُهُمْ أى وصفهم العجيب الشأن في الكتابين جميعا، ثم ابتدأ فقال كَزَرْعٍ يريد: هم كزرع. وقيل: تم الكلام عند قوله ذلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ ثم ابتدئ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ ويجوز أن يكون ذلك إشارة مبهمة أوضحت بقوله كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ كقوله تعالى وَقَضَيْنا إِلَيْهِ ذلِكَ الْأَمْرَ أَنَّ دابِرَ هؤُلاءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُصْبِحِينَ. وقرئ: الإنجيل، بفتح الهمزة شَطْأَهُ فراخه. يقال: أشطا الزرع إذا فرخ. وقرئ: شطأه، بفتح الطاء. وشطأه، بتخفيف الهمزة: وشطاءه، بالمدّ. وشطه، بحذف الهمزة ونقل حركتها إلى ما قبلها. وشطوه، بقلبها واوا فَآزَرَهُ من المؤازرة وهي المعاونة. وعن الأخفش: أنه أفعل. وقرئ: فأزره بالتخفيف والتشديد، أى: فشدّ أزره وقوّاه. ومن جعل آزر أفعل، فهو في معنى القراءتين فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فصار من الدقة إلى الغلظ فَاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ فاستقام على قصبه جمع ساق. وقيل: مكتوب في الإنجيل سيخرج قوم ينبتون نبات الزرع، يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر. وعن عكرمة: أخرج شطأه بأبى بكر، فآزره بعمر، فاستغلظ بعثمان، فاستوى على سوقه بعلىّ. وهذا مثل ضربه الله لبدء أمر الإسلام وترقيه في الزيادة إلى أن قوى واستحكم، لأنّ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قام وحده. ثم قوّاه الله بمن آمن معه كما يقوى الطاقة الأولى من الزرع ما يحتف بها مما يتولد منها حتى يعجب الزرّاع.
Question
If you say: His words 'that He may enrage the disbelievers through them' are a reason for what?
فإن قلت: قوله لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ تعليل لماذا؟
Answer
I say: for what their likening to the plant indicates of their growth, their progress in increase and strength; and it is possible that He gives as its reason 'God has promised those who believed,' because when the disbelievers hear of what is prepared for them in the hereafter, together with how He makes them mighty in this world, that enrages them. The meaning of 'among them' is explanatory, like the words of the Exalted 'so avoid the filth of idols' (al-Hajj 22:30). From the Messenger of God, may God's blessing and ﷺ and his family: 'Whoever recites Surat al-Fath, it is as though he were among those who witnessed with Muhammad the conquest of Mecca.'
قلت: لما دل عليه تشبيههم بالزرع من نمائهم وترقيهم في الزيادة والقوّة، ويجوز أن يعلل به وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لأنّ الكفار إذا سمعوا بما أعدّ لهم في الآخرة مع ما يعزهم به في الدنيا غاظهم ذلك. ومعنى مِنْهُمْ البيان، كقوله تعالى فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم «من قرأ سورة الفتح فكأنما كان ممن شهد مع محمد فتح مكة» «2» .
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 346
1. (1) . His words 'that He will make your religion prevail (dinak)' probably should read 'his religion (dinahu),' as al-Nasafi's wording. (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «إنه سيظهر دينك» لعله: دينه، كعبارة النسفي. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 347
1. (1) . His words 'wa-l-akhlaq al-sajiha' i.e., the easy. Stated by al-Sihah. (Editor)
2. . His words 'thafanat al-ba'ir': in al-Sihah: they are what touches the ground of its limbs when it kneels. (Editor)
3. . His words 'la ta'lubu suwarakum': in al-Sihah: 'alabtuhu a'libuhu (with damma): when I marked it or scratched it or left a trace on it. (Editor)
4. . I did not find it as a raised hadith, and it is, in what follows it, a statement stopping at a Companion.
5. . 'Abd al-Razzaq related it from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Habib, from Abu al-Tha'tha', from Ibn 'Umar: 'that he saw a man scraping (yantahizu) when he prostrated, and said: Do not turn your form over (la taqlib).' He means: do not mark it. I said: What is 'do not turn your form over'? He said: do not change, do not disfigure. And Ibrahim al-Harbi related it from the narration of Abu Mu'awiya from al-A'mash from Habib from 'Ata' from 'Umar: 'that he saw a man on whose face prostration had left a mark, and said: do not turn your form over.' Then he said: qalabtu al-shay' when you leave a trace on it. [.....]
6. . His words 'laysa bi-l-nadb in the faces': in al-Sihah, 'al-nadb' is the trace of a wound when it does not rise above the skin. (Editor)
1. (1) . قوله «والأخلاق السجبحة» أى السهلة. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قوله «ثفنات البعير» في الصحاح: هي ما يقع على الأرض من أعضائه إذا استناخ. (ع)
3. . قوله «لا تعلبوا صوركم» في الصحاح: علبته أعلبه- بالضم-: إذا وسمته أو خدشته، أو أثرت فيه. (ع)
4. . لم أجده مرفوعا وهو في الذي بعده موقوف.
5. . أخرجه عبد الرزاق عن الثوري. عن الأعمش عن حبيب عن أبى الثعثاء. عن ابن عمر «أنه رأى رجلا ينتحز إذا سجد فقال: لا تقلب صورتك» يقول لا تؤثرها. قلت: ما تقلب صورتك؟ قال: لا تغير لا تشن» ورواه إبراهيم الحربي من رواية أبى معاوية عن الأعمش عن حبيب عن عطاء عن عمر «أنه رأى رجلا قد أثر السجود بوجهه فقال: لا تقلب صورتك. ثم قال: قلبت الشيء إذا أثرت فيه. [.....]
6. . قوله «ليس بالندب في الوجوه» في الصحاح «الندب» : أثر الجرح إذا لم يرتفع عن الجلد. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 348
1. (1) . Ibn Maja related it from Isma'il al-Talhi from Thabit ibn Musa from Sharik from al-A'mash from Abu Sufyan from Jabir as a raised hadith with this. The imams of hadith, Ibn 'Adi, al-Daraqutni, al-'Uqayli, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim, agreed that it is Sharik's own statement, which he said to Thabit when he entered. And Ibn 'Adi said: a group stole it from Thabit, such as 'Abd God ibn Shubruma al-Sharikay and 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahr and others. The author of Musnad al-Shihab cited it from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq from al-Thawri and Ibn Jurayj from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, and it is fabricated by this chain. Likewise from the narration of al-Husayn ibn Hafs from al-Thawri from al-A'mash from Abu Sufyan from Jabir, and the matter in it is the same; and by other feeble routes. Ibn Tahir said: al-Qudaa'i thought the hadith authentic because of the many routes; he is excused because he was not a hafiz. It has other routes not from the narration of Jabir: Ibn Jumay' gave it in his mu'jam from the hadith of Anas, and Ibn al-Jawzi by another route from him, and it is false by both routes as well.
2. . Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi related it with the chain to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
1. (1) . أخرجه ابن ماجة عن إسماعيل الطلحي عن ثابت بن موسى عن شريك عن الأعمش عن أبى سفيان عن جابر مرفوعا بهذا واتفق أئمة الحديث وابن عدى والدارقطني والعقيلي وابن حبان والحاكم على أنه من قول شريك قاله لثابت لما دخل. وقال ابن عدى سرقه جماعة من ثابت كعبد الله بن شبرمة الشريكى وعبد الحميد بن بحر وغيرهما وأورده صاحب مسند الشهاب من رواية عبد الرزاق عن الثوري وابن جريج عن أبى الزبير عن جابر وهو موضوع على هذا الاسناد. وكذا من رواية الحسين بن حفص عن الثوري عن الأعمش عن أبى سفيان عن جابر والأمر فيه كذلك. ومن طرق أخرى واهية. قال ابن طاهر: ظن القضاعي أن الحديث صحيح، لكثرة طرقه. وهو معذور لأنه لم يكن حافظا. وله طرق أخرى من غير رواية جابر أخرجه ابن جميع في معجمه من حديث أنس وابن الجوزي من وجه آخر عنه وهو باطل أيضا من الوجهين.
2. . أخرجه ابن مردويه والواحدي بالإسناد إلى أبى بن كعب.
